answer: Since Chicago is where you're residing, the standard setup is ComEd for electricity and Peoples Gas for gas, with water and trash billed through the City of Chicago — and for internet you're mostly choosing between Xfinity, AT&T Fiber, and Astound/RCN, so check availability by your exact address since fiber coverage varies block to block. For groceries, Jewel-Osco and Mariano's are the big local chains, Aldi and Trader Joe's are the cheaper staples run, and the neighborhood farmers markets are worth a look if you want to keep that fresh-from-the-farm habit going. One more to knock out the same week: a City of Chicago vehicle sticker and residential parking permit if you're keeping a car there, since those tie back to the address you've been updating everywhere.
